chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Miskan, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The charity (zakat) of the Emigrants (Muhajirun) is not permissible for the Bedouins, nor is the charity of the Bedouins permissible for the Emigrants.

key_terms.الْمُهَاجِرِينَ: The Emigrants (referring to those who migrated with the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on giving zakat from Muhajirun to A'rab (Bedouins)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the administrative boundaries of zakat distribution, reflecting the early Islamic practice of maintaining distinct fiscal categories for settled urbanites (Muhajirun) and nomadic Bedouins (A'rab). Shia scholars interpret this as a safeguard against the misappropriation of funds, ensuring that zakat collected from specific demographic groups is utilized within their own communities rather than being transferred across different social or residential sectors.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It is not Permissible, a charity (Zakāt) of the Emigrant for the Bedouins, nor a charity (Zakāt) of the Bedouins for the Emigrants’.
en.sarwar: 10. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan from al- Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Zakat of immigrants (converts to piety and religion) is not lawful for Arabs and the charity (Zakat) of Arabs is not lawful for immigrants.’”
